overview: Sierra Leone is a country on the Atlantic coast of West Africa. Its capital and largest city, Freetown, was founded in the late 1700s as a home for freed enslaved people. Sierra Leone became independent from the United Kingdom in 1961. A civil war from 1991 to 2002 caused great suffering, and the country is rich in diamonds.

geography.text: Sierra Leone has a coast of mangrove swamps and beaches, with the mountainous Freetown Peninsula. Inland are plains and plateaus, rising to mountains in the east, where Mount Bintumani is the highest peak. Heavy rain falls during the rainy season.

history.text: Temne and Mende peoples lived in the region, and the coast was part of the slave trade. In 1787 British campaigners founded Freetown as a home for freed slaves, and it became a British colony. Sierra Leone became independent in 1961. A brutal civil war from 1991 to 2002 was fought partly over diamonds, and an Ebola epidemic struck in 2014.

events.title: Freetown
events.text: A settlement for freed slaves is founded.

events.title: Civil war
events.text: A war begins that lasts eleven years.

government.text: Sierra Leone is a presidential republic. Since its civil war ended in 2002, it has held regular elections, with power changing hands peacefully in 2007 and 2018.

economy.text: Mining of iron ore, diamonds, rutile and gold dominates exports. Most people farm, growing rice and cassava.

culture.text: Krio, an English-based creole, is spoken by nearly everyone. The Cotton Tree in Freetown was a symbol of the city for centuries until a storm toppled it in 2023. Bunce Island is a former slave-trading fort.

items.title: Krio
items.text: The common language of Sierra Leone.

sport.text: Football is the most popular sport. The national team is nicknamed the Leone Stars.
